title: Yemen's Four-Year Truce Collapses as Houthis Seize Mocha; Grundberg Warns UN Security Council of 'Dangerous Phase'
detail: September 10, 2026 — Houthi forces captured the strategic Red Sea port city of Mocha, the last harbour fully under the internationally recognised government's control, extending an offensive launched September 3 across Taiz, Hodeidah, Al-Jawf and Al-Bayda governorates and bringing the group within reach of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, through which 10-12% of global trade passes. UN Special Envoy for Yemen Hans Grundberg told an emergency UN Security Council session that Yemen faces 'a new and more dangerous phase of war' as the fragile truce in place since April 2022 collapses, warning that fighting has displaced more than 11,400 households (roughly 44,000 people) and that consequences 'will not remain within Yemen's borders.' The escalation follows Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia that wounded 73 civilians on September 8 — described by the Houthis as retaliation for a Saudi strike that killed seven in Al-Jawf — and comes atop a UN estimate of 18.3 million Yemenis facing acute food insecurity. Yemen's UN ambassador condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia; Saudi Arabia's ambassador called for enforcement of UN Resolutions 2216 and 2722. Grundberg urged the Houthis to halt attacks on commercial shipping and civilians and called for the political settlement track to be preserved despite the fighting.

title: Quintet Concludes First-Ever Khartoum Mission, Rejects 'Parallel Governing Structures' as RSF Pursues Rival Administration
detail: September 10, 2026 — The Quintet (African Union, United Nations, IGAD, League of Arab States, European Union) concluded its three-day, first-ever joint Good Offices mission to Khartoum, meeting SAF commander and Sovereignty Council chairman Abdelfattah al-Burhan, Prime Minister Kamel Idris, the Democratic Bloc Alliance and the Sudanese-Sudanese Dialogue Preparation Committee. In a closing statement, the bloc said 'there is no military solution to the conflict in Sudan' and explicitly rejected any 'parallel governing structures' — a direct rebuke of the Rapid Support Forces' effort to stand up a rival administration separate from the internationally recognised government — while reaffirming 'full respect for Sudan's sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity.' AU representative Mohamed Ibn Chambas called the talks 'constructive'; PM Idris said the dialogue process is 'the property of the Sudanese people' and pledged government cooperation; Darfur regional governor Minni Minawi stressed any dialogue must remain entirely Sudanese-led and free of external or militia pressure. The mission builds on UN Personal Envoy Pekka Haavisto's parallel push for a negotiated settlement as 'the only viable path' to a comprehensive ceasefire.

title: Israel Blows Up Major Hezbollah Tunnel Network Beneath Ali Taher Ridge, Triggering 4.1-Magnitude Tremor, as Rome Talks Loom
detail: September 10, 2026 — The IDF destroyed what it called a major Hezbollah tunnel network beneath the Ali Taher ridge in southern Lebanon using more than 1,100 tonnes of explosives, an operation Israeli officials said completed a 'security zone' along the ridge; the US Geological Survey recorded a 4.1-magnitude tremor from the blast. Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz said in a joint statement the tunnel complex — spanning over two kilometers and functioning as the 'nerve center' of Hezbollah's Badr regional division — held Iranian-made rockets, missiles, drones, anti-tank weapons and mines, and was intended to support a possible incursion into Israel's Galilee. The strike lands days before the next round of US-brokered Israel-Lebanon talks, tentatively set for Rome next week (Tuesday or Wednesday, per an Israeli official), where the disputed Hezbollah-disarmament 'pilot zones' issue is set to stall until after Israel's October elections. A US State Department official separately urged Lebanon to 'formulate a plan for disarmament in all Lebanese territory,' welcoming south Lebanese communities' calls for their government to assert sovereignty over Hezbollah weapons storage.
